papers.title: Your Transformer Can Hold Two Thoughts at Once: Evidence of Linear Superposition in LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate the Superposition Linearity Hypothesis in Transformers, showing that linearly combined input streams yield a superposition of individual next-token distributions, which can be disentangled during decoding to generate two coherent continuations simultaneously.
key_points: Superposition linearity is an intrinsic structural property of the Transformer architecture rather than an emergent feature of pretraining, and it diminishes as pretraining advances.
Lightweight fine-tuning can substantially restore linearity by reducing the divergence between the actual superposed output distribution and the average of the individual distributions.
A novel guided decoding procedure successfully disentangles superposed outputs, permitting two distinct, coherent text continuations from a single model forward pass.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables the generation of multiple distinct, coherent text streams simultaneously from a single forward pass while establishing foundational insights into linear representation mechanics in LLMs.

papers.title: Rufus-Air: An Open LLM Post-Training Recipe

summary.tldr: Rufus-Air introduces an open, reproducible eight-stage post-training pipeline for GLM-4.5-Air-Base (106B-A12B) that relies entirely on open-source components and public data without new human annotations or distillation teachers.
key_points: Organizes post-training into an eight-stage serial pipeline: SFT, Reasoning RL, Coding RL, Instruction-Following RL, General Agent, Coding Agent, Search Agent, and RLHF.
Orders RL stages based on reward reliability, transitioning systematically from hard verifiable rewards to softer judge-based signals.
Uses difficulty filtering to maintain RL prompts within a productive learning range and relies on high-quality SFT to establish a strong capability floor.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that advanced open-weights models can outperform official releases using fully open data, public tools, and structured post-training without proprietary teachers or manual annotations.

papers.title: RGBD20K: A Large-Scale Benchmark for RGB-D Semantic Segmentation

summary.tldr: RGBD20K is a large-scale RGB-D semantic segmentation benchmark featuring 20,000 image pairs, 160 fine-grained categories, re-evaluated high-fidelity annotations, and a novel score-purified fusion (SPF) method.
key_points: Dataset scale includes 20,000 RGB-D image pairs, significantly expanding available training resources compared to prior benchmarks.
Expands semantic coverage to 160 fine-grained classes, surpassing NYUv2 (40 classes) and SUN RGB-D (37 classes).
Establishes a high-fidelity ground truth through rigorous re-evaluation and correction of existing annotation noise.
Introduces Score-Purified Fusion (SPF), achieving state-of-the-art multimodal RGB-D semantic segmentation performance across evaluated benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a cleaner, significantly larger, and more diverse RGB-D dataset alongside a novel fusion method to advance highly generalizable multimodal semantic segmentation models.

papers.title: Learning to Discover Interesting Mathematics

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a metric defining mathematical interestingness as proof length divided by statement length, training a 27B model to score proof difficulty and autonomously discover novel, non-redundant theorems.
key_points: Intrinsic interestingness is formally defined as the ratio between proof length and statement length, which strongly correlates with downstream theorem utility.
A 27B parameter model was trained to predict premise-conditioned proof difficulty, outperforming general-purpose frontier models on this task.
Optimizing for the new metric reduced full or substantial overlap between generated theorems and Mathlib from 91.9% to 30.6%, producing significantly more out-of-distribution math.
The system iteratively selects interesting candidate theorems to construct a self-expanding, machine-verified mathematical library without human-supplied targets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated, self-improving formal reasoning systems to discover and catalog non-trivial, original mathematical knowledge without relying on human guidance.

papers.title: ExplorationBench: Measuring AI Systems' Exploration in Verifiable Alien Worlds

summary.tldr: ExplorationBench is a framework evaluating AI exploration using verifiable, executable Alien Worlds where rule sets conflict with pre-training data to prevent memorization.
key_points: Features two sandboxes: AlienCode (31 discovery targets, 70 tasks) and AlienLogic (24 discovery targets, 70 tasks).
Provides flawed manuals, environmental feedback, and dedicated tool-call schemas to guide system exploration before solving held-out tasks.
Evaluation of 10 AI systems showed performance varied across trajectories, with continued exploration sometimes stalling or reversing initial gains.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a concrete, verifiable method to test if AI systems can discover and apply genuinely new knowledge rather than relying on memorized pre-training data.

papers.title: FLEET: From Logits Entropy to Enhanced Trajectories in Text Generation

summary.tldr: FLEET introduces a memory mechanism that uses high-entropy state trajectories from prior LLM generations to infer per-token utility scores, steering generation and reducing redundant semantic outputs.
key_points: Replaces memoryless temperature sampling by tracking sparse trajectories of states where logits entropy exceeds a predefined threshold.
Uses trajectory history to compute per-token utility scores that dynamically adjust logits during generation.
Matches standard repeated sampling accuracy with a 3x speedup under equal budget constraints.
Boosts deterministic greedy-decoding Pass@32 performance on LiveCodeBench from 59.9% to 66.2%.
Requires minimal pipeline modifications, deriving its primary hyperparameters through a single calibration pass.
summary.why_it_matters: FLEET enables faster, deterministic inference and significantly higher pass rates on complex coding benchmarks without requiring additional sampling overhead or extensive architectural changes.

papers.title: Six Layers Less: Encoder Pruning for Whisper with Label-Free Recovery

summary.tldr: A layer-pruning approach removes six encoder layers from Whisper using leave-one-layer-out WER ranking, combined with label-free monolingual distillation to recover accuracy without requiring custom inference code.
key_points: Ranks Whisper encoder layers by the leave-one-layer-out change in Word Error Rate (WER) and removes the six least impactful layers, pruning 18.5% of the encoder stack.
Uses unlabeled monolingual speech distillation to reduce mean WER across four languages from 21.9% (zero-shot pruned) down to 20.1%, compared to an 18.2% baseline.
Produces a standard shallow encoder model that requires no custom inference implementations to achieve speedups.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables lightweight, standard-compliant deployment of optimized Whisper models by compressing the encoder architecture alongside existing decoder-pruned variants.

papers.title: AV-GRPO: Modality-Anchored Decoupling Diffusion Reinforcement Learning for Joint Audio-Video Generation

summary.tldr: AV-GRPO introduces a modality-anchored online diffusion reinforcement learning framework and the 5DAV dataset to improve joint audio-video generation quality, semantic alignment, and cross-modal synchronization.
key_points: Uses modality-anchored rollouts to disentangle learning signals, stabilize training difficulty, and isolate multimodal rewards into unimodal subproblems.
Employs trajectory-locked frozen-tower optimization to reduce computational overhead and improve credit assignment across audio and video modalities.
Applies adaptive objectives and perturbation strengths customized to the distinct dynamics of individual modalities.
Introduces 5DAV, a training dataset decoupled across five dimensions to enable difficulty-controllable training.
Outperforms LTX-2.3 in generation quality, semantic alignment, and audio-video synchronization under both LoRA and full fine-tuning setups on JavisBench and VABench.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves reward entanglement and high computational costs in multimodal reinforcement learning, enabling more precisely synchronized and higher-fidelity joint audio-video generation.

papers.title: Uranus: Building the Next-Generation Simulation Infrastructure for Embodied AI

summary.tldr: Uranus is a data-driven robot simulator using a joint-trajectory-conditioned autoregressive diffusion model for real-time, streaming frame generation across varied robot embodiments.
key_points: Uses a joint-trajectory-conditioned autoregressive diffusion architecture to process online joint-position inputs without a fixed horizon.
Generates one latent frame per step (mapping to four RGB frames) and reaches 24 FPS following inference optimization.
Provides a unified interface for synchronized multi-view frame generation supporting diverse camera configurations and robot embodiments.
Evaluated on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution control scenarios, with model weights and code publicly released.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables low-latency, scalable simulation for robot policy training and data generation without requiring manual, labor-intensive scene construction.

papers.title: EmbodiedSWE: Coding Agents for Long Horizon Dexterous Robotics

summary.tldr: EmbodiedSWE introduces a framework and benchmark for evaluating coding agents on long-horizon robotic tasks and converting their verified solutions into scalable training data for vision-language-action (VLA) models.
key_points: EMBODIEDSWE-BENCH tests coding agents on contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects, and tasks requiring up to 30 minutes of continuous interaction.
Frontier coding agents successfully solve long-horizon tasks and transfer code solutions across different tasks and robot embodiments through iterative interaction.
EMBODIEDSWE-GEN expands single agent-generated code solutions into diverse trajectory datasets to train VLA policies.
Finetuning a VLA exclusively on agent-generated simulation demonstrations enables successful real-world deployment on a long-horizon task.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that coding agents can autonomously generate high-quality, diversified simulation data to scale supervision and train real-world generalist robot policies without manual teleoperation.

papers.title: Just Ask Jev: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions as a Zero-Shot Detector of AI Alignment Failures

summary.tldr: Jev, a model trained via reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions (RLCD), achieves zero-shot alignment failure detection across 10 failure types in a single pass at 63x lower cost than LLM judges.
key_points: Evaluated on RLCDAlignBench, spanning 44 benchmarks, 10 alignment failure types, and 5 target models using both benchmark scorers and human labels.
A single generic question asked to Jev achieves a median AUROC of 0.886 zero-shot, outperforming supervised baselines on most benchmarks.
Detects relational alignment failures by varying input context fields separately from question wording and answer types.
Matches the agreement rate of reference scorers with human labels and identifies existing benchmark label defects while offering a 63x cost reduction compared to LLM-as-a-judge approaches.
summary.why_it_matters: RLCD-based models like Jev provide a highly efficient, cost-effective alternative to multi-token LLM judges for real-time monitoring of diverse AI alignment failures.

papers.title: ViRDM: Taming Representation Distribution Matching for Few-Step Causal Video Generation

summary.tldr: ViRDM is a generator-only post-training recipe for few-step causal video generation that eliminates teacher and critic networks by using representation distribution matching.
key_points: Eliminates the three-network DMD architecture by matching generator outputs to a precomputed target distribution without an online critic or teacher model.
Resolves memory bottlenecks in multi-step causal rollouts via stochastically truncated clean-exit supervision, a lightweight VAE decoder, and staged vector-Jacobian products.
Introduces lightweight dynamics regularization alongside optimized generated-population and initialization regimes to enforce temporal consistency.
Achieves an 84.87 score on the official VBench evaluation using 20 generator updates, taking 16 A100 GPU-hours.
summary.why_it_matters: It drastically reduces memory and compute overhead for training low-latency streaming video models by removing teacher-critic stacks during distillation.

papers.title: DeltaWAM: Delta World Action Models for Bimanual Manipulation

summary.tldr: DeltaWAM introduces a world-action model that predicts visual deltas rather than dense future frames and uses Streaming Delta Memory to accelerate inference for bimanual robot manipulation.
key_points: Uses three streams (dense-anchor, sparse-delta, and action) across three distinct architectures to decouple dynamic changes from static visual appearances.
Streaming Delta Memory (SDM) updates cached anchor context using compact observed deltas, avoiding full-frame video expert re-processing during inference.
Reduces training FLOPs by 17.78% to 23.77%, while SDM lowers single-step inference latency by 36.57% and inference FLOPs by 31.55%.
Outperforms Fast-WAM on RoboTwin, increasing average success rates from 81.3% to 85.4% in clean settings and from 75.8% to 83.9% under visual randomization.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly lowers computation costs and inference latency for video-generator-based robot control while improving policy robustness against visual distractions.

papers.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation

summary.tldr: A study calls for integrating calibration as a standard evaluation criterion alongside standard performance metrics across all NLP benchmarks to prevent deployment risks and pipeline failures.
key_points: Standard calibration metrics require only a confidence score and a correctness judgment per example, inputs that most current benchmarks already collect.
Miscalibration introduces failure points in deployment via overconfident errors and in research pipelines like LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic data generation, and active learning.
Defining confidence and correctness inputs for open-ended generation remains an unsolved challenge.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating confidence alongside accuracy ensures model outputs are trustworthy in real-world deployments and prevents cascading errors in automated research pipelines.

papers.title: X-Planner: Event-Structured Task Planning for Embodied Intelligence

summary.tldr: X-Planner introduces an event-structured planning front-end for VLA systems using hierarchical multi-source data and dual discrete/latent plan interfaces decoded via Staircase Decoding.
key_points: Combines Ego, UMI, and teleoperation data structured under a granularity hierarchy with takeover-time annotations to supervise ongoing error recognition.
Exposes a discrete plan interface for interpretable event states and a latent interface that relays continuous CoT states across staggered Transformer depths.
Utilizes Staircase Decoding alongside a frozen latent-to-text reconstruction objective to anchor the semantic space of the continuous representations.
Demonstrated superior performance against evaluated baselines in real-robot execution and ranked second out of four models in offline BERTScore-F1 and judge-based evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves long-horizon robotic manipulation by providing explicit, structured intermediate planning representations that enhance both text-level reasoning quality and downstream real-robot execution.

papers.title: Robust Detection of LLM-Generated Text under Contamination

summary.tldr: A statistical framework modeling human and machine text as Huber-contaminated Markov processes establishes theoretical boundaries for LLM text detection and proves that clipping likelihood-ratio tests restores detector consistency under editing and contamination.
key_points: Models text sources as finite-order Markov processes under Huber contamination to establish an exact theoretical boundary where detection transitions from impossible to reliable.

Proves that raw additive score detectors lose all worst-case power under sufficient contamination, whereas clipped likelihood-ratio tests maintain consistency and vanishing worst-case error rates below the detection boundary.
Empirically tested across seven detectors, three datasets, three generation models, and the RAID benchmark, showing consistent robustness improvements.

Demonstrates that clipping increases the log-likelihood-log-rank ratio (LRR) detector's true-positive rate at a 5% false-positive rate by a median of 8.3 percentage points in controlled settings, and 2.1 to 4.3 points on RAID benchmark evaluations.
summary.why_it_matters: Clipping provides a simple, theoretically grounded modification that prevents adversarial editing and text contamination from completely degrading existing LLM detection algorithms.

papers.title: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance

summary.tldr: SAGE introduces a framework combining algebraic sparsification and hyperbolic structural guidance to mitigate exploration and compounding biases in long-horizon LLM reasoning.
key_points: Identifies two main failure modes in long-horizon reasoning under sparse rewards: exploration bias toward unstable local branches and compounding bias from accumulated local deviations.
Introduces Symbolic Closure Analysis (SCA) to theoretically characterize how branching structures induce reasoning biases under local admissibility.
Applies algebraic sparsification to project candidates onto operator-indexed algebraic subspaces, reducing spurious branching.
Uses hyperbolic structural guidance to embed reasoning states into negatively curved space, providing dense depth-wise signals.
Demonstrates performance gains across 12 benchmarks and 7 model families, including an 8-fold improvement on the Andrews-Curtis problem.
summary.why_it_matters: SAGE provides a principled methodology to prevent large language models from derailing during complex, multi-step problem solving where feedback is extremely sparse.

papers.title: Style, Not Self: Surface Cues Explain Zero-Shot Code Attribution by Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Evaluations reveal that LLM zero-shot self-recognition and self-preference are driven by surface cues like length and formatting, disappearing almost entirely after rule-based code normalization.
key_points: In single-solution self-recognition tests across MBPP, HumanEval, and DS-1000, LLMs achieved only 49-58% balanced accuracy, with raw accuracy driven by authorial claim bias.
Pairwise self-attribution accuracy correlates strongly (r=0.93) with output length differences between the evaluator and the opponent model.
Rule-based normalization removing docstrings, comments, type hints, and local names reduces 10 of 12 re-tested attribution results to chance level without degrading Pass@1 performance.
Normalizing code removes Claude Haiku's observed self-preference bias during evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM self-collusion and evaluation biases stem from simple surface-level stylistic markers rather than deep self-awareness, allowing straightforward normalization routines to mitigate self-preference bias.

papers.title: Canopy: Exploiting Piecewise Smooth Tree Priors for Multi-Fidelity Bandits

summary.tldr: CANOPY is a multi-fidelity tree bandit that constructs online certificates of local aggregation bias via cheap random-path probes to handle piecewise smooth optimization spaces in LLM inference.
key_points: Uses cheap random-path probes at internal nodes to build an online certificate of local aggregation bias.
Directs expensive leaf evaluations toward regions where the online certificate detects smoothness violations.
Provides theoretical guarantees with an additive regret cost based on the number of discontinuities, matching smooth-tree rates when violations are absent.
Achieves 2.9x higher top-10 recall in 1000-model routing, 1.6x more SWE-bench Verified issues resolved, and 3.6x lower median time-to-first-token in prefix caching.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient multi-fidelity optimization across LLM inference tasks by dynamically adapting to sharp boundaries without requiring pre-specified global smoothness schedules.

papers.title: Tracking States or Tracking Cosets? An Algebraic Account of Learned State Tracking

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that neural networks tracking group element updates learn to track subgroup cosets rather than full states, revealing distinct normal and non-normal coset tracking behaviors across Transformer and recurrent architectures.
key_points: Transformers exhibit quotient solutions where models predict quotient classes accurately while outputting nearly uniform probability distributions across individual class members.
For finite groups with uniform i.i.d. inputs, optimal order-blind exact accuracy converges to the reciprocal of the group's abelianization class size as prefix length grows.

A census shows Transformer coset partitions derive exclusively from normal subgroups, whereas parameter-matched recurrent networks transition through both non-normal and normal right-coset stages during training.
In recurrent networks trained on A5, low-dimensional 3D state subspaces encode non-normal cosets as approximate dodecahedra, allowing state swaps to transfer coset states through shared suffixes.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how models learn algebraic coset representations provides a mechanistic framework to explain partial accuracy, prefix-reordering failures, and architectural differences in sequence-tracking tasks.

papers.title: Mind What Matters for Reasoning: Aligning Cross-Modal Attention via Selective Probability Mass Concentration

summary.tldr: Selective Probability Mass Concentration (sPMC) improves MLLM visual reasoning by selectively regularizing text-to-image attention distributions in only 3%-15% of visually responsive attention heads using segmentation priors.
key_points: Identifies specific grounding-responsive attention heads using Adaptive Head Selection while leaving non-target heads unconstrained to preserve complementary functions.

Treats normalized attention over visual tokens as a spatial probability distribution and uses segmentation-derived spatial priors to concentrate probability mass onto semantically relevant image regions.
Improves implicit visual grounding to reduce hallucinations and language prior over-reliance without directly supervising the reasoning steps.
Achieves an average zero-shot accuracy improvement of 3% and maximum gains of up to 11.3% across 6 multimodal benchmark suites.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that regularizing a small fraction of visually responsive attention heads significantly boosts MLLM reasoning accuracy without requiring explicit reasoning-path supervision.

papers.title: Who Holds the Pen? Let Specifications, Not Agents, Sign Off

summary.tldr: SpecHarness decouples LLM agent proposal generation from completion authority by compiling task specifications into versioned obligation states validated by runtime evidence.
key_points: Identifies two failures in single-loop agents: the understanding-execution gap (understanding a requirement without satisfying it) and the state-authority gap (self-declaring completion without independent verification).

Empirical evaluation on SkillsBench across seven models reveals that completion-claim rates exceed official evaluator pass rates by 28.7 to 37.9 percentage points, with only 79.6% to 86.4% of task directions satisfied.

SpecHarness extracts 509 source-grounded task directions from prompts, workspaces, and injected skills, translating verifiable requirements into binding obligation states while leaving ambiguous requirements as advisory.
Restricts completion authority so that agents can only request completion, requiring admissible evidence from qualified providers to officially sign off on state transitions.
summary.why_it_matters: Preventing LLM agents from self-evaluating their own task completion eliminates false-positive success claims and enforces compliance in autonomous agent execution.

papers.title: The Alignment Illusion in Multimodal Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Standard scalar alignment metrics fail to detect visual token corruption in Multimodal Large Language Models because anisotropic language model MLP projections induce artificial visual-text similarity.
key_points: Across 13 MLLMs (0.5B to 72B parameters), replacing visual tokens with Gaussian noise severely degrades task performance, yet standard alignment metrics (CKA, SVCCA, MIR, and leading principal-angle cosine) fail to reliably distinguish noise from valid input.
This 'alignment illusion' stems from the shared language-model pathway, where anisotropic MLP down-projections pull visual and text tokens into common output directions regardless of visual content.

Because weight-induced alignment is predominantly one-dimensional, the authors introduce the principal-angle gap (PA gap)—the difference between the top two principal-angle cosines—to isolate multi-directional visual structure.
The PA gap tracks task accuracy under graded visual corruption more accurately than scalar metrics and reveals geometric discrepancies when models evaluate structured but irrelevant images.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating internal visual-text integration using standard scalar alignment metrics can be misleading; researchers must use structural geometric metrics like the PA gap alongside controlled task performance to reliably assess cross-modal processing.

papers.title: Do Audio Language Models Hear and Read Distinctive Features Alike?

summary.tldr: An analysis of six audio language models reveals that speech and text decoders rarely align distinctive feature directions across modalities, with only voicing in Qwen2.5-Omni exceeding random baseline references after statistical correction.
key_points: Evaluated feature representation alignment using mean vector offsets of minimal phoneme pairs across 6 models, 7 phonological features, and 15 languages from 11 families.
Only the voicing feature in two Qwen2.5-Omni models demonstrated cross-modal directional alignment above the random-pairing reference baseline after multiple testing correction.
Voicing maintained a consistent cross-lingual direction in the audio stream across 14 languages in three models, with complete language-pair agreement in two models.
Reference baseline values varied by a factor of seven across different models.
Cross-modal feature alignment is predicted by model family architecture rather than model size.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding that single-decoder audio language models process spoken and written phonological features along distinct directional paths informs how architecture family choice impacts cross-modal representation transfer.

papers.title: Return or Revise? Learning When Revision Helps Retrieval-Augmented QA

summary.tldr: A new framework trains policies on paired correctness outcomes to predict a revision's recoverability, improving decision accuracy on whether to return or revise draft answers in retrieval-augmented QA.
key_points: Evaluates draft answers and candidate revisions under the same judge to observe repair, harm, and oracle gaps before revision.
A recoverability scorer outperforms a draft-correctness scorer across all nine Llama setup-seed fits, adding 0.23-0.68 accuracy points on average and closing over a third of the oracle gap.
The policy still incurs a 38-46% rate of harmful revisions.
Selecting between a draft and a draft-free standard-RAG answer outperforms adding a third candidate-revision option by ~2 accuracy points for Llama and ~4 points for OLMo.
summary.why_it_matters: Predicting revision recoverability allows QA systems to selectively query retrieved evidence, improving overall answer accuracy while reducing unnecessary or harmful revisions.

security.title: Storm-3168: Agentic-driven cloud attacks using compromised service principals

summary.tldr: Microsoft tracked threat actor Storm-3168 using compromised Azure service principals to execute agentic AI-orchestrated cloud recon, resource destruction, and credential collection across multiple services.
key_points: Compromised service principals performed extensive enumeration using the user agent python-requests/2.34.2, including mapping VMs, subscriptions, and App Service configuration stores.
A seven-minute destructive sequence included 100+ Azure Storage account deletion attempts alongside 150+ total destructive or credential collection operations in 35 minutes.
Targeted Azure components included Storage Accounts, SQL databases, Key Vaults, Function Apps, Virtual Machines, App Services, and recovery protection locks.
Azure resource locks and storage account-level deletion protections successfully blocked a subset of the deletion attempts.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how threat actors use automated agentic workflows to execute post-compromise cloud destruction at high speed, underscoring that exposed service principal credentials remain actionable until explicitly revoked or rotated.

security.title: The Fly That Stopped: Mushroom-Body-Inspired Habituation as a Reward-Free Scheduling Prior for Autonomous Penetration Testing

summary.tldr: A mushroom-body-inspired, reward-free habituation scheduler reduces duplicate tool selections in autonomous penetration testing without relying on scalar reward updates.
key_points: Uses sparse state encoding with decaying habituation counters across structural URL classes and tool families to penalize repeated outcomes.
Lowered duplicate-action ratios in 6 of 8 non-tied measurable lab targets (p=0.015625), cutting duplicate steps from 51 to 18 in a 60-step budget.
Evaluated local and readout plasticity on a 13,498-neuron MaleCNS-derived circuit (501,267 synaptic edges), finding local plasticity produced no action selectivity under a fixed readout.
Demonstrated that reward-driven components failed to outperform the reward-free MB condition due to reward-accounting errors and tool-failure loops.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that biological habituation mechanisms can prevent costly repetitive tool-failure loops and optimize action budgets in autonomous security testing without complex reward engineering.

security.title: TraceGuard: Adaptive Multimodal Poison Filtering through Cross-Feature Rank Agreement

summary.tldr: TraceGuard is an adaptive, training-free filtering method that detects multimodal data poisoning using rank agreement across six corpus-level features analyzing cross-modal neighborhoods, recurring text, and text-span erasure.
key_points: Analyzes collective poison influence via six corpus-level features without training the target model.
Uses cross-feature rank agreement and shared patterns to identify suspicious samples and adaptively determine removal thresholds without prior knowledge of the poison rate.
Evaluated across 19 attack configurations (image-text learning, VLM fine-tuning, encoder-transfer), removing an average of 98.4% of poisoned examples and 5.4% of clean examples.
Reduces the residual attack metric to 1% or less in 13 out of 19 tested configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: TraceGuard provides an effective, training-free defense to purge stealthy poison attacks from multimodal datasets before model training occurs.

security.title: The Tokens Remember: When Tokenization Bypasses Knowledge Editing and Unlearning

summary.tldr: Toketive is a reference-free attack that exploits alternative valid tokenizations of an input string to bypass LLM knowledge editing and unlearning, recovering pre-edit responses without needing the original model or auxiliary classifiers.
key_points: Model editing and machine unlearning evaluate modifications under canonical tokenizations, leaving a security gap where alternative valid tokenizations induce different computational trajectories.
Toketive operates solely on the released model without needing pre-edit models, training data, shadow models, or auxiliary classifiers.
Across five LLMs, six datasets, and six editing/unlearning methods, 38.6% of alternative tokenizations successfully bypass modifications to recover pre-edit responses.
Toketive detects modified facts with an F1 score of 84.2% (a 26.2% relative gain over the top baseline) and reconstructs pre-edit responses with 74.5% top-5 accuracy (a 21.7% gain).
summary.why_it_matters: Localized model edits and unlearning techniques cannot be considered secure knowledge-control boundaries without evaluating model behavior against adversarial alternative tokenizations.

security.title: Calibrated Decision Models for Autonomous Penetration-Testing Harnesses: JEV and Laya as System One Decision Layers for LLM-Driven Pentest Agents

summary.tldr: This paper proposes using non-generative System One decision models (Jev, Laya, and the proposed Rave) to improve finding adjudication, severity recalibration, agent pruning, and confirmation loops in autonomous LLM-driven penetration-testing harnesses.
key_points: Identifies four target decision points for non-generative models in pentest harnesses: finding adjudication, severity recalibration, agent pruning, and confirmation loops.
Presents an exploratory NeuroSploit case study on a web target with 13 vulnerabilities, comparing execution with and without the Jev System One layer.
Reviews specifications for Jev, Jev-Ultrafast, and open-source Laya, and evaluates alignment training approaches including RLHF, RLAIF, RLCD, and RLHV for security contexts.
Proposes Rave, a domain-adapted System One decision model, detailing its training data requirements, evaluation protocol, and assurance impact.
summary.why_it_matters: Replacing generative LLMs with calibrated, lightweight classifiers for decision points reduces false positives, prevents severity inflation, and optimizes compute usage during automated security assessments.

security.title: On the Effectiveness of Kernel-Level Evidence for Agent Security

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Agent Cross-Layer Evidence (ACE), a corpus pairing application telemetry with kernel-level syscall traces to prove that combining cross-layer evidence improves LLM agent attack detection over single-layer telemetry.
key_points: ACE dataset contains 4,047 sessions across 17 threat models, 6 delivery vectors, 14 OWASP LLM/agentic threat categories, and 12 attack mechanics.
Kernel-level syscall traces capture malicious instructions and actions that bypass application-layer boundaries and remain invisible to traditional telemetry.

Evaluations across four detector families show that combining kernel and application evidence outperforms single-layer views, demonstrating generalization to unseen attacks and runtime transferability.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying solely on application-level telemetry leaves AI agent deployments vulnerable to evasive attacks that can only be detected at the OS kernel level.

security.title: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion

summary.tldr: Codetta is a high-capacity, keyless steganographic protocol enabling undetectable collusion between independently deployed, asymmetric multi-agent LLM systems without pre-shared secret keys.
key_points: Uses a shared public model to estimate communication channels, a distribution-preserving sampling mechanism, and an adaptive error-correcting code.
Eliminates pre-shared keys by introducing a steganographic key exchange that establishes shared keys in approximately 80k visible tokens with an empirical failure rate of at most 4.1e-3.
Achieves up to 94x the capacity of existing state-of-the-art asymmetric LLM steganography protocols while remaining computationally indistinguishable from benign transcripts.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that undetectable agent collusion is practically feasible across independent deployments, proving that text transcript inspection alone is insufficient for auditing multi-agent LLM security.

security.title: Progressive Skill Discovery as Access Control for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Structural Governance through Role-Scoped Capability Delivery

summary.tldr: Skilder is a framework that governs LLM tool use by dynamically serving role-scoped skills, tools, and constraints through a single Model Context Protocol (MCP) server based on progressive skill discovery.
key_points: Packages tools, skills, instructions, and execution boundaries into discrete role-scoped bundles.
Uses a single MCP server to deliver capabilities dynamically, ensuring tools are accessible strictly within discovered and authorized skills.
Provides deterministic, system-level enforcement that completely prevented unauthorized tool calls and parameter violations (e.g., spending limit breaches) across evaluations.
Evaluated across 13 tasks with 6 models (10 runs each), outperforming flat-context tool selection and multi-agent orchestration while allowing dynamic mid-task capability acquisition.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces probabilistic prompt-based safety guardrails with deterministic system-level access controls while simultaneously reducing context window overhead in large enterprise toolsets.

security.title: Decision Hijacking: Prompt Injection Attacks on Jev's Typed Probabilistic Decisions

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated prompt injection on Jev, a non-generative, typed probabilistic decision model, finding that while untrusted inputs shift action probabilities, successful decision hijacking remains rare.
key_points: Evaluated Jev using 510 reconstructed InjecAgent test cases to measure prompt injection impact on schema-defined non-generative outputs.
Malicious content shifts action probabilities, but standard attacks rarely cause the model to select the target action; override markers reduce influence and contextual claims show small effects.
Adaptive attacks using score feedback doubled the mean highest attacker-target probability during optimization, but validation success on fresh calls only increased from 1.8% to 3.5%.
Successful attacks correlate with small initial decision margins or instances where the attacker exercises greater control over the input observation.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that schema-constrained, non-generative models alter but do not fully eliminate prompt injection vulnerabilities, necessitating risk evaluations for probabilistic action selection.

security.title: BRFID: Toward Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection

summary.tldr: BRFID demonstrates that uncoordinated label-flipping attacks in a federated intrusion detection system cause adversarial self-degradation, providing a detectable signal for identifying Byzantine clients without needing data exfiltration.
key_points: Label-flipping poisoning (60% flipped labels) by a single Byzantine client reduced its own accuracy from 99.96% to 84.33% in a three-client setup on the CICIDS2017 dataset.
The global ensemble maintained stable accuracy across all tested poisoning rates despite non-IID attack subtype distributions and no active defense mechanisms.
The experiments evaluated a non-parametric Federated Forest (tree concatenation) aggregation rather than parametric FedAvg.
summary.why_it_matters: The self-inflicted performance drop caused by label-flipping attacks creates a reliable behavioral anomaly that can be exploited to detect Byzantine clients in federated learning environments.

security.title: Agent Approval Laundering: Transitive Effects Beyond the Approved Invocation

summary.tldr: Researchers identify approval laundering in coding agents, where human-approved commands omit transitive workflow effects, and demonstrate mitigation using effect-bound records containing source-backed predictions.
key_points: Formalized approval laundering as a record-coverage failure across six effect classes, proving that record-only policies cannot guarantee safety due to identical policy-visible fields requiring different decisions.
Evaluated residual unrecorded effects across 111 approval-object/trace pairs, reducing residual records from 40 using explicit fields down to 13 when incorporating decision-time metadata.
Achieved zero metadata residuals across 11 fixed-SHA executions, with two exact mappings recurring across three different product frontends.
Implemented prospective recovery via frozen source-backed predictions, achieving 0.926 macro recall and 0.941 macro precision on 17 holdout workflows while cutting residual effects from 10 to 3.
Integrated the system into Claude Code's PreToolUse to pass frozen records through the permission path without requiring automatic approval.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that truthful invocation logging is insufficient for AI agent security, requiring authorization policies to evaluate pre-computed predictions of an action's full transitive execution boundary.

security.title: Persistent Billable State: Denial-of-Wallet Attacks and Defenses in Tool-Calling LLM Agents

summary.tldr: This study introduces persistent billable state in tool-calling LLM agents, demonstrating Denial-of-Wallet attacks where retained tool outputs inflate cumulative input usage up to 14,293x across six model families.
key_points: Retaining raw tool outputs in session history increases the mean effective session cost by 21.2% to 35.9%.
Introduces DOW-BENCH to evaluate six Denial-of-Wallet attack vectors across 243 executions, showing peak input expansion of 14,293x compared to initial prompt size.

Proposes a host-side kernel combining deterministic history transformation with four invariants (bounding prompt mass, context growth, recursive opportunity, and cumulative spend) that contained all 123 attack replays.
Demonstrates that a progress-authorized host policy achieves 22/24 task completions without pre-completion interruptions on Mistral Small 4, outperforming fixed caps (13/24).
Audit of 3,830 MCP repositories revealed only 71 contained code-visible safeguard proxies, with zero repositories covering all four required safeguard families.
summary.why_it_matters: Malicious tool outputs can covertly drain API budgets through repeated context re-ingestion, requiring host runtimes to implement pre-reingestion history transformation and bound invariants.

security.title: The Vulnerability of Neural Audio Watermarks under Speech Enhancement

summary.tldr: Cascading Gaussian noise with speech enhancement models creates a black-box attack that effectively removes neural audio watermarks, with generative speech enhancement proving particularly destructive.
key_points: Evaluated a black-box watermark removal attack cascading Gaussian noise with both discriminative and generative speech enhancement (SE) models.
Tested the attack against six neural watermarking methods: AudioSeal, WavMark, SilentCipher, Timbre, Perth, and AlignMark.
Generative SE models destroy watermarks highly effectively by reconstructing speech harmonic regions during the denoising process.
Outperformed existing neural re-synthesis techniques in watermark removal success.
summary.why_it_matters: Speech enhancement models expose a critical security vulnerability in commercial AI-generated speech tracing systems, requiring watermark developers to incorporate SE-aware robustness evaluations.

security.title: DistillGuard: Malicious NPM Package Detection and API Attack Chain Analysis via Static Graph and LLM Distillation

summary.tldr: DistillGuard detects malicious NPM packages by extracting multi-granular static graph features and fine-tuning an offline Qwen3-8B model using LoRA with knowledge distilled from an online LLM.
key_points: Uses three static analysis modules to extract multi-granular graph semantic features from NPM packages across installation, import, and execution stages.
Distills security knowledge and structured labels from an online LLM to fine-tune an open-source Qwen3-8B model using LoRA for secure, offline deployment.
Achieves 95.3% accuracy, 99.4% precision, and a 93.8% F1 score, outperforming baseline tools by 11.1 to 30.0 F1 percentage points.
Identifies eight typical API attack chains and analyzes malicious behavior distributions across NPM attack stages.
summary.why_it_matters: DistillGuard provides an accurate, offline-deployable defense against NPM supply chain attacks without exposing sensitive code to third-party LLM APIs.

security.title: Control the Harness, Control the Cost: Routing and Governing AI Coding Agents in the Enterprise

summary.tldr: Researchers built Jev, a calibrated prompt classifier router that optimizes enterprise AI agent harness routing to save 14% to 21% on model costs while mitigating single-vendor dependencies.
key_points: Jev labels every user prompt against a custom taxonomy to govern model selection, prompt caching, and subagent execution.
The router restricts model switching to session starts, side lanes, and subagent launches to prevent cache rebuilding overhead across turns.
Repricing 10,000 real agent sessions showed that on long, tool-heavy tasks, top-tier models cost less than mid-tier models due to prompt caching mechanics.
Emulating a 10,000-seat deployment using Anthropic's September 2026 pricing yields enterprise savings between $3.3M and $5.0M annually.
summary.why_it_matters: Enterprises can deploy a self-hosted control plane over third-party coding agent harnesses to lower LLM spending and avoid vendor lock-in.

infra.title: Scaling MoE reinforcement learning on Amazon EKS with EFA and DeepEP with 40% more throughput

summary.tldr: AWS demonstrates an optimized architecture for scaling Mixture-of-Experts reinforcement learning on Amazon EKS using Elastic Fabric Adapter and DeepEP to achieve 40% higher throughput.
key_points: Addresses the high communication overhead of Expert Parallelism (EP) dynamic all-to-all token routing alongside TP, DP, and PP in MoE models.
Balances heterogeneous compute demands between rollout generation (large-scale distributed inference) and policy training in RLHF/PPO and GRPO pipelines.
Uses DeepEP over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) on Amazon EKS to optimize inter-node expert-parallel communication and eliminate training bottlenecks.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves training efficiency and accelerator utilization for ultra-sparse MoE models, significantly reducing post-training times for complex RL workflows.

infra.title: Accelerate multimodal RL training with SkyRL on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

summary.tldr: AWS demonstrated using SkyRL on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with EKS to post-train a Qwen3-VL-8B vision-language model via GRPO, improving its maze solve rate from 43.75% to over 95%.
key_points: Post-training used Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on a VisGym SFT checkpoint for multi-turn visual maze navigation with sparse rewards.

Required infrastructure includes SageMaker HyperPod on EKS, ml.g7e.12xlarge and ml.r5d.16xlarge instances, KubeRay operator, and FSx for Lustre for shared checkpointing and LoRA adapter synchronization.
SageMaker HyperPod provides automated node health monitoring and replacement to protect multi-node RL rollout progress during hardware failures.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a resilient, scalable cloud architecture for multi-turn reinforcement learning on multimodal models without losing training progress to infrastructure failures.

infra.title: Multi-Region training with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and Qumulo

summary.tldr: AWS and Qumulo introduced a solution combining Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with Cloud Native Qumulo and Cloud Data Fabric, enabling cross-Region model training without replicating datasets or sacrificing GPU utilization.
key_points: Uses Cloud Native Qumulo (CNQ) and Cloud Data Fabric (CDF) with NeuralCache to predictively cache cross-Region data locally over NFS via VPC peering.
Validated between us-east-2 (hub/data) and us-west-2 (spoke/compute) across 60 ms of network latency.
Spoke throughput converged to match the local hub's performance at 115–117 samples/sec within 100–150 initial batches.
Sustained 98–100% GPU utilization and sub-3 ms data operations on p5.48xlarge instances after the initial warmup phase.
summary.why_it_matters: AI teams can train models on GPU clusters located in different AWS regions without migrating petabytes of data or taking long-term training throughput penalties.

infra.title: Deploying real-time personalized speech with Qwen3-TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI

summary.tldr: The Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base text-to-speech model is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart for real-time, self-hosted voice cloning deployment.
key_points: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base uses the Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz speech tokenizer and supports 10 languages, streaming generation, and cross-lingual cloning from a few seconds of audio.
Voice cloning works without retraining by processing a reference audio clip, its transcript, and the new target text to match timbre, pitch, and cadence.
SageMaker JumpStart also includes the Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice (predefined voices) and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B models for deployment via the SageMaker Python SDK.
Self-hosting on managed SageMaker real-time endpoints keeps audio data within the user's AWS account and shifts pricing from per-character API fees to compute usage.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can deploy zero-shot voice cloning capabilities directly within their AWS environment while retaining data control, avoiding per-character API costs, and managing infrastructure via SageMaker.

infra.title: Scribd, Inc. classifies more than 400 million documents with Gemini batch inference on Gemini Enterprise

summary.tldr: Scribd, Inc. used Gemini Enterprise batch inference on Google Cloud to automatically classify over 400 million user-uploaded documents.
key_points: Scribd processed a catalog of over 400 million user-uploaded documents using Google Cloud.
The classification system utilized Gemini Enterprise and its batch inference capabilities to handle large-scale document processing.
summary.why_it_matters: Batch inference with Gemini Enterprise enables large-scale, automated content organization and classification for enterprise libraries containing hundreds of millions of files.

summary.tldr: Meta's Muse provides a consumer-accessible agentic AI system that runs dedicated, persistent Linux virtual machines per user in the cloud.
key_points: Muse provisions a full, individual, persistent Linux virtual machine in Meta's cloud for each user.
The system delivers a consumer-accessible, agentic AI interface packaged with an easy-to-use installer and mascot.
John Gruber highlights significant safety risks, noting consumers likely lack awareness of the agent's power and potential dangers, particularly when executed on a Mac.
summary.why_it_matters: Packaging powerful agentic systems with persistent root access behind friendly consumer interfaces creates significant security and safety risks for unaware users.

summary.tldr: Working extensively with coding agents demonstrates that they increase software engineering difficulty by requiring extraordinary discipline and knowledge to unlock their full potential.
key_points: Coding agents enable powerful capabilities in software engineering but increase the overall difficulty of the discipline.
Fully leveraging coding agents requires developers to possess high levels of technical knowledge and strict operational discipline.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers cannot rely on coding agents as a shortcut, as successfully using them demands greater domain expertise and rigorous practice.

vendors.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to Southeast Asia and Taiwan

summary.tldr: OpenAI has expanded ChatGPT Ads availability to Southeast Asia and Taiwan, enabling eligible businesses in these regions to run advertisements across over 60 countries.
key_points: Geographic expansion of ChatGPT Ads into Southeast Asia and Taiwan.
Enables eligible regional businesses to serve ads across more than 60 countries.
summary.why_it_matters: Eligible businesses in Southeast Asia and Taiwan can now leverage ChatGPT's global user base across 60+ countries for targeted ad campaigns.
